newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: No refinery turnaround plans for Malaysia in 1997.
newsitem.headline: No refinery turnaround plans for Malaysia in 1997.

text.p: Malaysia's refiners do not have any major plans to shutdown any of its 388,000 barrel-per-day refining capacity for turnarounds in 1997, industry sources said on Friday.
"The schedule for the next fiscal year (April 1997-March 1998) has not been decided," said a source.

Sources said state-owned Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) had no plans to shut refinery capacity up to March 1997 with the exception of a ten-day shutdown at its 100,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) Malacca refinery from December 1.
Decisions on whether to shut any refinery space after March 1997 has yet to be decided, industry sources said.
The Royal Dutch Shell Company said it had no plans for either of its 105,000-bpd Port Dickson refinery on the west coast of peninsular Malaysia of its 45,000-bpd Sarawak refinery in East Malaysia.
Esso will skip turnarounds at its 88,000-bpd refinery at Port Dickson next year, with the next scheduled for 30 days in March 1998.
